key_themes: Brand refresh initiative with new 'Fortuna Wave' visual identity focused on Authenticity, Prosperity, and Togetherness (APT) to enhance recognition and differentiation
Strategic investment from Blackstone received board and shareholder approval, validating strategy and governance while strengthening capital base and providing access to global expertise
Structural shift in balance sheet mix toward mid-yield assets and improved liability franchise driving margin expansion and sustainable profitability
CASA growth momentum strongest in industry at 6.59% QoQ and 18.86% YoY, with CASA ratio improving to 32.07% (up 106 bps QoQ)
Focus on risk-adjusted profitability and consistency over headline growth, with disciplined balance sheet management across rate cycles

Structural transformation through four strategic levers: strengthening NIMs via CASA growth (especially current accounts), improving asset mix toward medium-yield products, building diversified fee income, and maintaining strong asset quality
NIM expansion exceeded guidance, improving from 2.94% to 3.06% driven by 19 bps lower deposit costs and strategic CASA ratio improvement of 120 bps year-over-year
Deliberate portfolio rebalancing away from low-yield assets (corporate and home loans representing ~50% of book) toward medium-yield segments like commercial banking, CV finance, LAP, and gold loans
MFI stress peaked in Q1 but continues to impact results, though easing month-over-month; rest of asset book remains stable with no other asset quality concerns
Fee income resilience demonstrated with 13% Q-o-Q growth despite muted treasury income, crossing 1% fee-to-assets milestone for first time

Federal 4.0 transformation strategy focused on three core objectives: improving CASA (especially current accounts), driving better yield on advances through asset mix reshaping, and increasing granularity and volume of fee income
Branch network optimization through 'Free The Branch' initiative with 70 regional business support centers operational and regional loan service centers being established in Q2
Technology modernization including corporate credit underwriting automation, FedOne unified interface for corporates, FedMobile app enhancements, and GenAI-powered chatbot in testing
Organizational restructuring across retail assets (separate heads for secured/unsecured), wealth management vertical established, and corporate banking B-FIG segment creation
Asset quality challenges primarily in MFI/Agri segments with gross slippages of Rs. 658.19 crore in Q1, though stress showing signs of peaking with declining trajectory in June-July
Strategic shift towards mid-yielding segments (mass affluent, MSME, LAP, gold loans) with 19% Y-o-Y growth achieved in medium-yield portfolio
Strong focus on liability franchise improvement with CA growing 27% Q-o-Q and 35% Y-o-Y, CASA ratio at 30.23%
Implementation of new operational frameworks including RaRoC-based pricing, transfer pricing methodology, and business-wise P&L system to drive accountability
Asset quality at decadal best with GNPA at 1.84% (down 11 bps Q-o-Q), NNPA at 0.44%, and provision coverage strengthened to 75.37%
Major organizational transformation initiatives including talent acquisition (9 of 14 N-2 positions filled), Operation Udaan for branch modernization, and brand refresh with Vidya Balan as ambassador
management_outlook: NIM expansion journey expected to continue for many quarters as CASA percentage grows and medium-yield assets grow faster than low-yielding segments, though next quarter will see 2/3 impact of recent rate cut
Credit cost guidance of 52-53 bps for full year FY26, improving from initial 55-60 bps guidance, with further improvement expected in Q4
MFI portfolio showing improving trajectory in slippages and credit costs quarter-over-quarter, but management remains cautious and will watch one more quarter before accelerating growth
Priorities remain unchanged: strengthening liability franchise, growing in chosen higher quality lending segments, and maintaining control on cost and asset quality
Too early to provide specific long-term targets for loan mix composition, but will continue journey of growing mid-yield book faster than high-yield book

Confident about continued NIM improvement beyond current 3.06% level through ongoing deposit repricing over next 6 months and sustained CASA momentum, though specific targets not provided due to multiple moving parts
Expect stronger growth momentum in LAP and BuB segments in coming quarters after reversing negative trends; committed to growing in chosen high-yield segments while maintaining profitability focus
Anticipate gradual easing of MFI stress but not yet in comfortable zone; credit costs expected to moderate but maintaining full-year 55 bps guidance with aspiration to come below
Wealth management, trade and forex revenue initiatives gaining momentum expected to further strengthen fee trajectory over next few quarters
Proactively took INR 46 crore management overlay on standard accounts with connected exposure stress as precautionary measure, demonstrating conservative approach
Expect NIMs to bottom out in Q2 (subject to no further rate cuts) and improve in H2 as cost of funds falls, with full year guidance of maintaining credit cost around 55 bps
Anticipate disbursement momentum to improve post-monsoon especially in retail and MSME, with growth targeted at 1.2x nominal GDP
MFI stress expected to linger at most one more quarter with peak slippages seen in May and declining trajectory in June-July
Strong opportunities identified in secured MSME, business banking, gold-backed lending, LAP and CVCE segments as medium-yielding focus areas

H2 expected to see stronger retail growth with restructuring complete and festive season momentum, combination of better macro, declining cost of funds, and unsecured lending recovery to support margin normalization
Confident in resuming gold loan growth following regulatory clarity after facing headwinds in Q4 due to regulatory issues
Plans to revive personal loan growth as credit environment stabilizes, while maintaining cautious approach to microfinance for at least 1-2 more quarters
Expects to achieve reasonable asset growth in FY26 driven by mid-yield segments, with current account acquisition running 50% higher than previous period
Positioned for self-sustaining franchise with strong capital position (CRAR 16.4%, CET1 15.04%) providing ample headroom for growth
Confident in maintaining NIM stability through proactive measures including T+90 reset for floating rate loans, fixed-rate car loans, and recent deposit rate adjustments
analyst_concerns: Margin outlook sustainability given strong 24 bps expansion over last two quarters and impact of rate cuts, with clarification sought on repricing timeline
Distribution fee income was not very strong this quarter, raising questions about momentum in fee-generating businesses
MFI credit costs currently at 10-11% level and sustainability of overall credit cost improvement once MFI normalizes relative to lower costs in other segments
Quantitative guidance on future loan mix composition across high/mid/low yielding segments over 3-5 year horizon
MSME asset quality concerns and potential impact from US tariffs on commercial banking portfolio
Loan growth at 1.5% Q-o-Q significantly below system, questioning ability to meet 1.2x nominal GDP growth target for the year given deliberate slowdown in low-yield segments
Sustainability of CASA ratio improvements when overall balance sheet growth accelerates, as current low growth environment is helping maintain elevated CASA ratios
Timing and necessity of capital raise given improving margins and potential for self-funding growth through internal accruals, especially with consolidation in capital-light businesses
MFI asset quality stress continuation despite peak being reached in Q1, with questions about timeline for normalization and impact on credit costs
Potential impact of new RBI guidelines on ECL provisioning and revised standardized approach for operational and credit risk on capital ratios
MFI stress bunching in Q1 for Federal Bank while other lenders recognized it earlier in Q3-Q4, with questions about accelerated provisioning impact and duration of elevated credit costs
Broader stress emerging in retail segments including unsecured, business banking, and CV segments with questions about new stress build-ups and sustainability of credit costs
NIM compression due to faster repricing on T+1 basis with 100 bps rate cuts, questions about magnitude and duration of further margin decline in Q2 before stabilization
Competitive intensity especially on pricing and ability to maintain risk-adjusted profitability in current environment
Geopolitical and tariff-related uncertainties affecting the external environment despite improving macro backdrop
Whether bank can return to high-teen loan growth in FY26 after consolidation in lower-yield segments like home loans and corporate banking
Stickiness of year-end CASA growth, particularly whether strong Q4 current account growth of 27% Q-o-Q will be retained
NIM pressure from expected repo rate cuts and high EBLR book exposure (over 50% linked to external benchmark), seeking clarity on margin floor for FY26
One-off costs in Q4 OpEx including branch expansion (39 of 85 branches opened in Q4), campaigns and card-related expenses leading to uptick in cost-to-income ratio
Sustainability of fee income growth which outpaced asset growth, and whether this can continue as revenue diversification strategy

concall_themes: Brand refresh initiative with new 'Fortuna Wave' visual identity focused on Authenticity, Prosperity, and Togetherness (APT) to enhance recognition and differentiation
Strategic investment from Blackstone received board and shareholder approval, validating strategy and governance while strengthening capital base and providing access to global expertise
Structural shift in balance sheet mix toward mid-yield assets and improved liability franchise driving margin expansion and sustainable profitability
CASA growth momentum strongest in industry at 6.59% QoQ and 18.86% YoY, with CASA ratio improving to 32.07% (up 106 bps QoQ)
Focus on risk-adjusted profitability and consistency over headline growth, with disciplined balance sheet management across rate cycles

Structural transformation through four strategic levers: strengthening NIMs via CASA growth (especially current accounts), improving asset mix toward medium-yield products, building diversified fee income, and maintaining strong asset quality
NIM expansion exceeded guidance, improving from 2.94% to 3.06% driven by 19 bps lower deposit costs and strategic CASA ratio improvement of 120 bps year-over-year
Deliberate portfolio rebalancing away from low-yield assets (corporate and home loans representing ~50% of book) toward medium-yield segments like commercial banking, CV finance, LAP, and gold loans
MFI stress peaked in Q1 but continues to impact results, though easing month-over-month; rest of asset book remains stable with no other asset quality concerns
Fee income resilience demonstrated with 13% Q-o-Q growth despite muted treasury income, crossing 1% fee-to-assets milestone for first time

Federal 4.0 transformation strategy focused on three core objectives: improving CASA (especially current accounts), driving better yield on advances through asset mix reshaping, and increasing granularity and volume of fee income
Branch network optimization through 'Free The Branch' initiative with 70 regional business support centers operational and regional loan service centers being established in Q2
Technology modernization including corporate credit underwriting automation, FedOne unified interface for corporates, FedMobile app enhancements, and GenAI-powered chatbot in testing
Organizational restructuring across retail assets (separate heads for secured/unsecured), wealth management vertical established, and corporate banking B-FIG segment creation
Asset quality challenges primarily in MFI/Agri segments with gross slippages of Rs. 658.19 crore in Q1, though stress showing signs of peaking with declining trajectory in June-July
Strategic shift towards mid-yielding segments (mass affluent, MSME, LAP, gold loans) with 19% Y-o-Y growth achieved in medium-yield portfolio
Strong focus on liability franchise improvement with CA growing 27% Q-o-Q and 35% Y-o-Y, CASA ratio at 30.23%
Implementation of new operational frameworks including RaRoC-based pricing, transfer pricing methodology, and business-wise P&L system to drive accountability
Asset quality at decadal best with GNPA at 1.84% (down 11 bps Q-o-Q), NNPA at 0.44%, and provision coverage strengthened to 75.37%
Major organizational transformation initiatives including talent acquisition (9 of 14 N-2 positions filled), Operation Udaan for branch modernization, and brand refresh with Vidya Balan as ambassador
analyst_concerns: Margin outlook sustainability given strong 24 bps expansion over last two quarters and impact of rate cuts, with clarification sought on repricing timeline
Distribution fee income was not very strong this quarter, raising questions about momentum in fee-generating businesses
MFI credit costs currently at 10-11% level and sustainability of overall credit cost improvement once MFI normalizes relative to lower costs in other segments
Quantitative guidance on future loan mix composition across high/mid/low yielding segments over 3-5 year horizon
MSME asset quality concerns and potential impact from US tariffs on commercial banking portfolio
Loan growth at 1.5% Q-o-Q significantly below system, questioning ability to meet 1.2x nominal GDP growth target for the year given deliberate slowdown in low-yield segments
Sustainability of CASA ratio improvements when overall balance sheet growth accelerates, as current low growth environment is helping maintain elevated CASA ratios
Timing and necessity of capital raise given improving margins and potential for self-funding growth through internal accruals, especially with consolidation in capital-light businesses
MFI asset quality stress continuation despite peak being reached in Q1, with questions about timeline for normalization and impact on credit costs
Potential impact of new RBI guidelines on ECL provisioning and revised standardized approach for operational and credit risk on capital ratios
MFI stress bunching in Q1 for Federal Bank while other lenders recognized it earlier in Q3-Q4, with questions about accelerated provisioning impact and duration of elevated credit costs
Broader stress emerging in retail segments including unsecured, business banking, and CV segments with questions about new stress build-ups and sustainability of credit costs
NIM compression due to faster repricing on T+1 basis with 100 bps rate cuts, questions about magnitude and duration of further margin decline in Q2 before stabilization
Competitive intensity especially on pricing and ability to maintain risk-adjusted profitability in current environment
Geopolitical and tariff-related uncertainties affecting the external environment despite improving macro backdrop
Whether bank can return to high-teen loan growth in FY26 after consolidation in lower-yield segments like home loans and corporate banking
Stickiness of year-end CASA growth, particularly whether strong Q4 current account growth of 27% Q-o-Q will be retained
NIM pressure from expected repo rate cuts and high EBLR book exposure (over 50% linked to external benchmark), seeking clarity on margin floor for FY26
One-off costs in Q4 OpEx including branch expansion (39 of 85 branches opened in Q4), campaigns and card-related expenses leading to uptick in cost-to-income ratio
Sustainability of fee income growth which outpaced asset growth, and whether this can continue as revenue diversification strategy
management_outlook: NIM expansion journey expected to continue for many quarters as CASA percentage grows and medium-yield assets grow faster than low-yielding segments, though next quarter will see 2/3 impact of recent rate cut
Credit cost guidance of 52-53 bps for full year FY26, improving from initial 55-60 bps guidance, with further improvement expected in Q4
MFI portfolio showing improving trajectory in slippages and credit costs quarter-over-quarter, but management remains cautious and will watch one more quarter before accelerating growth
Priorities remain unchanged: strengthening liability franchise, growing in chosen higher quality lending segments, and maintaining control on cost and asset quality
Too early to provide specific long-term targets for loan mix composition, but will continue journey of growing mid-yield book faster than high-yield book

Confident about continued NIM improvement beyond current 3.06% level through ongoing deposit repricing over next 6 months and sustained CASA momentum, though specific targets not provided due to multiple moving parts
Expect stronger growth momentum in LAP and BuB segments in coming quarters after reversing negative trends; committed to growing in chosen high-yield segments while maintaining profitability focus
Anticipate gradual easing of MFI stress but not yet in comfortable zone; credit costs expected to moderate but maintaining full-year 55 bps guidance with aspiration to come below
Wealth management, trade and forex revenue initiatives gaining momentum expected to further strengthen fee trajectory over next few quarters
Proactively took INR 46 crore management overlay on standard accounts with connected exposure stress as precautionary measure, demonstrating conservative approach
Expect NIMs to bottom out in Q2 (subject to no further rate cuts) and improve in H2 as cost of funds falls, with full year guidance of maintaining credit cost around 55 bps
Anticipate disbursement momentum to improve post-monsoon especially in retail and MSME, with growth targeted at 1.2x nominal GDP
MFI stress expected to linger at most one more quarter with peak slippages seen in May and declining trajectory in June-July
Strong opportunities identified in secured MSME, business banking, gold-backed lending, LAP and CVCE segments as medium-yielding focus areas

H2 expected to see stronger retail growth with restructuring complete and festive season momentum, combination of better macro, declining cost of funds, and unsecured lending recovery to support margin normalization
Confident in resuming gold loan growth following regulatory clarity after facing headwinds in Q4 due to regulatory issues
Plans to revive personal loan growth as credit environment stabilizes, while maintaining cautious approach to microfinance for at least 1-2 more quarters
Expects to achieve reasonable asset growth in FY26 driven by mid-yield segments, with current account acquisition running 50% higher than previous period
Positioned for self-sustaining franchise with strong capital position (CRAR 16.4%, CET1 15.04%) providing ample headroom for growth
Confident in maintaining NIM stability through proactive measures including T+90 reset for floating rate loans, fixed-rate car loans, and recent deposit rate adjustments
